title: George Washington University (GWU)
summary: George Washington University (GWU) is a university in Washington. This entry compiles College Scorecard figures and related sources; UniRepository is not affiliated with GWU.

sections.heading: Key strengths
paragraphs: George Washington University (GWU) is a private nonprofit institution, as indicated by its ownership classification. One of the key strengths of GWU lies in its health-related programs, which constitute approximately 12.79% of its academic offerings. This focus highlights the university's commitment to advancing education and research in health fields. Notably, GWU does not offer programs in education, reflecting a specialized academic portfolio. The university's status as a private nonprofit institution supports its mission to provide quality education and foster innovation across its areas of expertise.

sections.heading: Popular majors
paragraphs: George Washington University (GWU) offers a diverse range of academic programs, with business studies being the most popular, accounting for about 14.28% of its academic share. Health-related programs also represent a significant portion, making up approximately 12.79% of the university's offerings. Computer-related majors constitute around 4.2%, reflecting GWU's engagement with technology and computing disciplines. Public administration programs are less prominent, comprising roughly 0.73% of the academic portfolio. Notably, GWU does not provide programs in education, indicating a focused selection of majors aligned with its institutional priorities.

sections.heading: Undergraduate admissions
paragraphs: Undergraduate admissions at George Washington University (GWU) are moderately selective, with an admission rate of approximately 47.09%. The university considers a range of academic credentials during the application process. Successful applicants typically present a strong academic record, with an average SAT score of 1433. GWU evaluates candidates holistically, though specific details about early decision or the use of the Common Application are not provided. Prospective students are encouraged to review the university's official admissions resources for comprehensive information.

sections.heading: How to read GWU tuition
paragraphs: George Washington University (GWU) charges a tuition fee of $67,710 for both in-state and out-of-state students, reflecting a uniform tuition policy regardless of residency status. This tuition cost represents the base amount required for enrollment in academic programs. However, the total cost of attendance at GWU is higher, amounting to $83,856. This figure includes additional expenses such as fees, room and board, books, supplies, and personal costs, providing a more comprehensive estimate of the financial commitment required for a student to attend the university.

sections.heading: Financial aid
paragraphs: Financial aid at George Washington University (GWU) includes support for students through various programs, with approximately 15.82% of undergraduates receiving Pell Grants. The median debt for students who complete their degrees at GWU is $20,449, reflecting the typical borrowing amount upon graduation. Prospective students can use the university's net price calculator available on the official GWU website to estimate their individual financial aid packages and out-of-pocket costs. Additional financial data and comparisons can be accessed through the College Scorecard link provided by the U.S. Department of Education.

sections.heading: Career outcomes
paragraphs: Career outcomes for graduates of George Washington University (GWU) indicate a strong return on investment. The university has a completion rate of approximately 83.98% within 150% of the normal time to degree, reflecting a high level of student persistence and success. Median earnings for GWU graduates are notable, with alumni earning around $71,607 six years after entry and increasing to $90,873 ten years after entry. These figures suggest that GWU graduates experience significant income growth as they advance in their careers. Additionally, the median debt for students who complete their degrees at GWU is $20,449, providing context for the financial investment required to attain these outcomes. Overall, these data points illustrate the potential economic benefits associated with earning a degree from GWU.
